analysis.execSummary: Total tracked spend of $1,003,655 has driven 38,357 wallet creations ($26.17 each) and 1,793 attributed connections ($560 each), returning $3.71M CLV against spend — 3.7×. The program earns its keep in aggregate, but in the measured Meta week (10 Aug) $4,990 of $7,493 wallet spend sat in ad-sets that produced nothing; the single most important action is to stop the $456Offer static and redirect the dead DoshCard and Bespoke money into the Conversions Mass ad-set that produced all 318 of the week's pooled wallets.
analysis.contentRead: messageThemes was truncated from this run, so message cannot be separated from channel; on the creative rail the 'Earn 1% DoshCard' and '$456 off' messages spent with zero wallets while the Wallet/Phone Dollars explainer pool carried all 318. A one-message-per-ad-set flight is the only way to separate message from ad-set objective.
keyFindings: CM360 whole-upload totals: $1,003,655 spend → 38,357 wallets at $26.17 and 1,793 connections at $560; CLV $3.71M, ROI 3.7×.
Meta week 10 Aug (platform workbook rail): $7,493 wallet spend, 320 wallets, and $4,990 (67%) of that spend sat in ad-sets producing zero wallets.
The 7-creative Facebook Conversions Mass ad-set produced 318 pooled wallets on $2,305 ($7.25/wallet) plus 4 immature pooled connections — the only thing working on Meta this week.
$456Offer static has exact attribution (1 creative per ad-set) and $4,045 across the board's Jun–Aug window with zero wallets; board verdict is 'watch', we recommend stop.
tierSpendSeries: wallet spend was cut ~70% on 1 July (~$3.7k/day → ~$1.1k/day) yet daily wallets held at ~90–130 — attribution may be crediting media for CRM/organic demand.
Base coverage: only 5.4% of 36,940 wallet creators appear in the consumer pay-monthly base export (an export property, not a media result); of those in base, 82.1% connected in-window.

whatsWorking.action: Hold and make it the destination for freed budget, but split the pool first — piling ~$5k/wk more into one ad-set will saturate its rate

analysis.incrementalityRead: The channels rail was truncated, so a search-vs-social creating/harvesting split cannot be made this run. The strongest incrementality signal present — wallets holding at ~90–130/day after the 1 July ~70% wallet-spend cut, with at-risk CRM stims starting 8 July — suggests attribution is being generous to paid media.
analysis.funnelRead: GA4 keys (trafficQuality, trafficSourceSplit, walletCreationSplit, ctaFriction) were truncated from this payload, so the landing→balance leak, click→session ratio, paid-vs-CRM session share, new-vs-existing wallet split and identify-flow friction are not measured this run.
analysis.crmOverlapRead: The July refreshed at-risk 60/90-day stim windows (8 Jul–Sep/Oct) and August High Risk (5–31 Aug) sit directly over the measured Meta week, with Bill Bonus SMS/EDM sends on 18–20 Aug. Paid cost-per-wallet figures in this window are flattered by CRM-driven creations media did not buy.
analysis.maturationRead: Median days-to-convert is 5 but the tail runs to 90 days, so the July and August cohorts (and this week's 4 pooled connections) are not yet judgeable. Re-read the August cohort in late October before treating any recent connection figure as final.
analysis.creativeRead: On the McCann platform workbook rail (week of 10 Aug only, never reconciled against CM360): the 7-creative Conversions Mass pool carried all 318 wallets while $4,990 of the week's $7,493 sat in zero-wallet ad-sets, and the highest click-rate creatives (Bespoke videos at 2.1–2.7%) produced nothing — engagement and wallets disagree outright. The creativeSignals rail for week of 17 Aug is empty with 36 wallet creatives outside feed coverage, so there are no deterministic flags to reconcile this run.
creativeTests: Split the 7-creative Conversions Mass ad-set into single-creative ad-sets — settles which of the seven earns the $7.25 pooled cost per wallet and which are passengers.
Run the DoshCard 'Earn 1%' creatives in a conversions-objective ad-set alongside the Traffic buy — settles whether the message or the awareness objective is why they bought zero wallets.
testsForNextFlight: Two-week media-dark or geo-split on Meta wallet spend during a stim-quiet window — settles how much of the ~90–130 daily wallets media actually causes after the July spend cut left volume flat.
One-message-per-ad-set flight (explainer vs $-off offer vs 1% earn) at equal budgets — settles whether message or ad-set structure drives the wallet gap.
Budget-split test on Conversions Mass at 1×/2×/3× current spend — settles the saturation point before the recommended ~$21.6k/mo of reallocations pile into it.
analysis.dataQualityNotes: This run's payload was truncated: placements, channels, campaigns, messageThemes, crossChannelFlows, weeklyRunRates, weeklySpendByPaybackTier, GA4 and walletUniverse were dropped entirely — treated as not measured, not zero, and they cap confidence at Low; tierSpendSeries is also cut off mid-July. feedQuality was not delivered, so the attribution ceiling cannot be graded this run. Creative grain exists on Meta only (no creative-grain data off Meta); 87.9% of measured board spend sits in multi-creative pools, including one 7-creative pool holding all 318 of the week's wallets, and creativeSignals for wk 17 Aug is empty with 36 wallet creatives outside spend-feed coverage. Single wallet-onboarding tag, no click/view-through split in this payload, no reach/frequency data for fatigue reads. Ask the agency to restore the full CM360 channel/placement export, the GA4 export, per-creative ad-set structure, and spend-feed coverage for the latest week.

body.content: Media — Verdict: Mixed, reallocate. The media page's analysis finds Wallet media returning 3.7× overall, but two-thirds of the week's $7.5k Meta wallet spend bought zero wallets — its highest-dollar action is to test the DoshCard Traffic ad-sets one more week and shift ~$10.3k/month into Conversions Mass if they stay dry (confidence: Low, driven by a truncated feed). Data-as-of date is unknown this run, so figures below are stated as at last refresh, not "this week". Spend - Last 7 days: $9,115 total ($1,302/day, GST-inclusive — do not gross up) vs prior 14-day average of $1,166/day, a modest step up in daily rate. Wallets and conversions - CM360 whole-upload totals: $1,003,655 spend produced 38,357 wallets at $26.17 per wallet. On Meta (week 10 Aug), $7,493 bought 320 wallets, with $4,990 (67%) sitting in ad-sets producing zero wallets; the 7-creative Facebook Conversions Mass pool delivered 318 of those wallets at $7.25. - Media-attributed network conversions (a subset of wallet creations, not wallets themselves): 653 in the last 7 days (93/day) vs 126/day prior, at $13.96 per conversion. Led by Wallet-PhoneDollars (394) and Meta (354). These figures will only improve as recent cohorts mature — conversion takes up to 30 days from wallet creation (~34% same-day, ~55% by 7 days, ~75% by 30 days), so current rates understate the final outcome; this is pipeline strength, not weakness. The fixed-window, same-weekday WoW trend is not available this run (weeklyRunRates truncated from the payload). - Additional-mobile and broadband attach rates: not available as at last refresh (not in this payload). Matured economics and pipeline health - Whole-upload matured view: 1,793 connections at $560 per connection; CLV $3.71M; ROI 3.7× (CLV ÷ spend). Judge return only on this matured window. - The pipeline is mixed rather than broken, per the analysis: one Meta ad-set is genuinely working, but the analysis also flags that wallet spend was cut ~70% on 1 July (~$3.7k/day → ~$1.1k/day) while daily wallets held at ~90–130 — attribution may be crediting media for CRM/organic demand. The sharp rise in raw conversion counts should be read through that caveat rather than as clean media efficiency. - In-flight pipeline (wallets created, not yet connected): not available as at last refresh (walletUniverse was truncated from this run's feed). - Best/worst channel and campaign by cost-per-matured-connection: not available this run — channels, placements and campaigns were truncated, so $1.00M of spend cannot be ranked by channel. At creative grain, the standout is the Conversions Mass pool ($7.25/wallet); the weakest is the $456Offer static ($4,045 over Jun–Aug, zero wallets, exact attribution). So What — Top 3 Recommendations: - Test then shift: Give DoshCard Traffic ad-sets one more measured week ($2,378 in wk 10 Aug, zero wallets — but a first-week awareness buy); shift ~$10.3k/month to Conversions Mass if still dry. - Stop the $456Offer static and shift its ~$8.0k/month into Conversions Mass — zero wallets on exact attribution goes past the board's "watch". - Fix the feed: restore the full CM360 channel/placement export, GA4, per-creative ad-set structure and latest-week spend coverage — until then, no portfolio-level reallocation can be sized and confidence stays Low. Cross-report connections: Cross-report connections: your zero-wallet Meta finding resolves a contradiction in the acquisition report, which attributed its prospect fall (238/day to 188/day) to reduced media spend — your data shows total spend rose ($1,166/day to $1,302/day) but $4,990 of $7,493 Meta wallet spend (67%) produced nothing, so effective spend fell while headline spend rose. Your $26.17 per wallet and $560 per matured connection also fill the unit-cost gaps acquisition could not state this run, with the caveat that your whole-upload window is broader than WIMW alone.
